column3: how to mark stable or unstable
Why does the compiler accept calling a mutating method on a vector when one of the arguments reads that same vector's length?
Before merging a risky compiler change, is there a way to try it against every published Rust package to see what stops working, and how long does that take?
How do standard library functions make a crash report blame the line in my code that called them rather than a line inside their own body?
My shipped binary still contains the folder on my laptop where I built it, including my username; can the compiler swap that out for something neutral?
If my outer build tool already caps how many things run at once, does rustc respect that cap or pick its own number of threads?
Is there a way to have the generated API reference show real call sites of each function, pulled from the sample programs bundled with my library?
What order should the fields go in at the top of my project's manifest, and where does the one-line blurb about the project belong?
#[cfg(bootstrap)] in a library the compiler depends on gives an unexpected cfg warning; what do I add to Cargo.toml to silence it?
//@ add-minicore: which compiler flags does it force on the test?
@rustbot: I rebased my PR after merge conflicts, how do I tell reviewers it's ready to look at again?
--cap-lints: is that why I never see warnings from my dependencies when cargo builds them?
avr-none: why do I still need avr-gcc installed if Rust already supports the target?
